newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia rescue plan seen stabilising Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Kia rescue plan seen stabilising Seoul stocks.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to stage a mild rebound on Monday on an anticipated package by financial institutions to bail out troubled Kia Group, brokers said.
Korean banks were to meet to discuss ways to rescue the natiion's eighth largest conglomerate, including financial aid and selling off group affiliates.
"People are expected to escape from the early Kia shock," said Cha Hee-gun at Sunkyong Securities. "And no selling pressure is seen in banking shares, which have bottomed out."
The composite stock index lost 5.22 points to 742.15 on Saturday.
But brokers said investors would shy away from some group shares with high debt-to-equity ratios, especially if their flagship company was performing badly.

They said investors would closely watch the outcome of the national convention by the ruling New Korea Party to select presidential nominee as the candidate would propose measures to revive the nation's economy.
